public_rationale: The claim is that people using false AI-generated content became more common over time. The best-tracked example is court filings with hallucinated citations. Damien Charlotin's database had 10 such rulings in 2023 and 37 in 2024. It then had 73 in just the first five months of 2025, with about 20 in May 2025 alone. That is a clear, fast rise in the period before the July 2025 post. No evidence found shows a flat or falling trend.
limitations: The evidence is a proxy from one domain, legal filings, not a measure of all botshit.
Counts of detected cases can rise because of more attention as well as more use.
The sentence is quoted from a 2024 article's abstract that Marcus endorses.
